chunks: And by this chain, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said regarding Laylat al-Qadr: “In it every wise matter is made distinct.”

He is saying: every wise matter descends in it, and the decisive matter is not two things; rather, it is one single thing. So whoever judges by that in which there is no disagreement, then his judgment is from the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and whoever judges by a matter in which there is disagreement, and considers himself correct, then he has judged with the judgment of al-Ṭāghūt.

Indeed, in Laylat al-Qadr the explanation of affairs descends, year by year, to the Walī al-Amr. In it, he is commanded regarding the matter of himself with such and such, and regarding the affairs of the people with such and such. And besides that, there occurs for the Walī al-Amr every day the special, concealed, wondrous, stored knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, similar to what descends during that night of the command.
Then he recited: “And if all the trees in the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas after it to replenish it, the Words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed Allah is Mighty, Wise.”

key_terms.أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ: a wise affair or decisive divine matter
key_terms.الطَّاغُوتِ: false authority or illegitimate judgment opposed to divine judgment
key_terms.الْمُحْكَمُ: that which is decisive, firm, and not subject to plurality or contradiction
key_terms.تَفْسِيرُ الْأُمُورِ: the detailed explanation or clarification of affairs
key_terms.حُكْمِ اللَّهِ: the judgment of Allah, the true divine ruling
key_terms.كَلِمَاتُ اللَّهِ: the Words of Allah, signifying His inexhaustible knowledge and command
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr, the night in which wise divine matters are distinguished and sent down
key_terms.وَلِيِّ الْأَمْرِ: the Master of the Command, to whom the affairs descend

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about Laylat al-Qadr and the descent of divine decree to the Walī al-Amr?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about Laylat al-Qadr as the night in which every wise and decisive matter is sent down. It presents these divine affairs as descending to the Walī al-Amr year by year, while also affirming that Allah’s knowledge remains inexhaustible and continually bestowed.
